details.detail: Sidewall panels and seams. Smooth satin wall with a joint mid-pier every second window, as in sp_py14. No gaps or z-fighting in s01, s02, s09 or win_*. Neutral white, where the photos are slightly warm (lighting).

F/J bowl. Width, pill button and grade are right: it is darkest just above the opening at 0.70 (photo 0.74). It reads well in s01, s05, s09 and b_jClose. The faint radial streaks from the pane's upper corners are less visible here than in the PY/Y tubs.

PY/Y tub. Proportions are unchanged from w6 (tub 0.83 of the pitch). The upper-tub grade is now 0.74-0.75 and the raised bezel ring reads. However, the grade is drawn as fan-shaped dark streaks radiating from the bezel's top corners into the tub (ra_yWin, b_pyClose, win_close). It looks like draped cloth rather than a smooth moulding.

Pane / lining / seal. Pane 36 x 54 px at a 79.4 px pitch in win_front, which is 0.243 x 0.36 m (spec 0.254 x 0.381 with slight perspective), so the ratio is right. The lining is graded grey with a channel line.

Electric shades. The sheer is right. The blackout is a believable warm grey with pleats, at 0.51 of the sill against 0.62-0.74 in the photos. A pale ~1.5 cm strip of lining shows below the closed blackout's bottom hem (b_jClose crop). omaat_room_24 shows pleats down to the opening edge.
Manual shades. The stowed band now reads, with a grip and a shadow line. The half and closed states in the studio are plausible.
Dado and grilles. Wide, low grilles with placards, dark dado and darker ribs. These match py_37303 and y_47303.

Floors. Carpets are unchanged and fine. The door-2 layout is now right (vinyl walkway, carpet in the bay). The vinyl is darker and more uniform than in sans_09: (75,74,80) against (105,100,105), and the stone-look mottle is missing.
Type A door surround and viewing window. The slot window is no longer covered by the arc. The leaf is still a flat slab; its moulding and bustle belong to monuments.

issues.detail: Radial dark streaks in the upper tub (new with the deeper w6 grade)
issues.problem: The sill / tub floor is a single ring loft from the lip ring straight to the opening ring (src/07_shell.js l.300, `sill = ringLoft([[inset(rr,0.019), D, mapE], [scl(open,1.085), D]], ...)`). tubShade (l.315) is evaluated only at those two rings. The opening's top vertices sit at the darkest value (fl 0.42 / 0.55) and the lip vertices are light, so long thin triangles interpolate the colour into fan-shaped streaks from the bezel's top corners. With fl at 0.42 this is now clearly visible as draped-cloth folds. The real tub is a smooth moulding with a soft vertical gradient (sp_py14, y_47303).
issues.evidence: ra_yWin x 400-520 / 580-730, y 250-300 (crop: rb7/cmp/yWin_crop.png); b_pyClose right window above the bezel; win_close tall tubs; faintly in the s01 F/J bowl (crop rb7/cmp/s01_crop.png).
issues.fix: Loft the sill through 4-6 intermediate rings so the vertex colour sampling is dense. Both rings come from the same `ths`, so lerp pointwise: `const sr=[0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1].map(t=>[inset(rr,0.019).map((p,i)=>[lerp(p[0],scl(open,1.085)[i][0],t),lerp(p[1],scl(open,1.085)[i][1],t)]), D, mapE]); const sill=ringLoft(sr,map,hint);`. Keep the normal override loop (it then needs wallAt per ring vertex: use `vc + pt[1]` for every ring). Optionally ease the grade with smoothstep instead of the linear ramp in tubShade so that no crease forms at d = oTop.

notes: The w7 renders are of head a746e65 (shell w6 fixes from both ratings), plus other workers' changes (monuments door furniture, lighting). Comparisons are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/0ed99896-ecef-596b-9423-893865e3345b/scratchpad/rb7/cmp/ (top = previous round, bottom = w7). Every w6 change helps: the F/J bowl and PY/Y tub grades, the stowed shade band, the bezel ring, the door floor split and the carpet hue. The blackout moved the right way but not far enough. The one regression is visual: the deeper grade exposes radial interpolation streaks in the sparsely tessellated tub floor. Studio note: in win_front the electric windows are on the LEFT and the manual PY/Y tubs on the RIGHT, the reverse of the brief's description. Lighting is not scored (white boarding mood neutralises the cream reveal).
